name: Primal Revolution guide series

lead: Primal Revolution is a numbered forum guide series on looksmax.org that collects a facial-structure programme in one place: tongue and lip posture, proper swallowing, sleep position, nasal and CO2 breathing, humming for nitric oxide, and a set of manual 'bonepulling' techniques. Its pitch is that environmental habits shape the maxilla, jaw and midface, so changing the habits can move them toward a more projected, defined look.

The series is community-authored and each part is a separate thread; readers on the forum respond with both interest and scepticism. No published study has tested the bonepulling or the combined programme for changes in adult facial bones.

paras: Readers follow the parts in order: oral posture and lip seal, a swallowing method the series calls the push-mush method, sleep habits, breathing practice, then progressive-stress exercises applied to the palate and cheek area. The author says the force should be light and progressive and that anything painful should be stopped. Users on the forum report running it alongside mewing.

Pressing on the palate, teeth and cheekbones can cause tooth, gum and jaw-joint discomfort, and orthodontists and craniofacial specialists describe adult facial bones as not changing shape under finger pressure. The series itself includes a disclaimer that its authors are not liable for losses or damages.

angle.text: Followers use the series as a daily-habit programme aimed at a more projected maxilla, wider palate and more prominent cheekbones. These outcomes are the series' own claims.

lead: Primal Revolution is a multi-part guide series posted on looksmax.org, numbered at least to part 19, covering oral posture, breathing, swallowing, sleep habits, the autonomic nervous system and manual bonepulling [1][2][3].

Its parts include maintaining a 24/7 lip seal [4], proper swallowing under a push-mush method [5], sleep habits said to prevent improper development [6], CO2 breathing [7], humming and nitric oxide [8], the stress role of the autonomic nervous system [9] and a discussion of eye shape, nose shape, recessed jaws, brow ridge, gonions and maxilla [10]. The later parts describe progressive-stress exercises such as thumbpulling, behind-the-teeth pulling, vomer pushing, towel pulling and zygo pushing [1][2][3][11][12].

The series belongs to the 'bonehacks' strand of looksmaxxing, which holds that habits and applied stress can change facial bone position. The wiki records the claims as the series states them; no published trial has examined the techniques.

paras: Each part is its own thread, and the numbering runs from foundations to techniques. Early and middle parts deal with habits: lip seal [4], swallowing [5], sleep [6], breathing [7], humming [8] and stress physiology [9]. A part on facial features discusses what the author calls proper development of eye shape, nose shape, jaws, brow ridge and maxilla [10].

Part 11 introduces what it calls progressive-stress-based exercises and part 12 covers conventional bonepulling in forward, lateral and reverse directions [11][12]. Later parts describe vomer pushing [13], behind-the-teeth pulling aimed at forward growth of the palate [3], external pull with maxilla relocation using a towel [2] and internal and external zygo pushing aimed at cheekbone width [1].

The author writes that the force should be the least possible and comfortable, that the method is not dangerous, and that anything painful should be stopped [2][3]. Specific technique details are not reproduced here.

Replies under individual parts range from requests for results to dismissal. One reader reply on part 19 says force would need to be applied around the clock to widen anything; another comment calls the threads unwanted [1][2].

Adult skull bones are not generally described by orthodontists or craniofacial surgeons as changing shape under light manual pressure, and no published study has tested thumbpulling, towel pulling or the programme as a whole. Related wiki entries on mewing and nasal breathing document the broader research on tongue posture and airway.

lore.intro: The series is part of looksmax.org's oral-posture and bonepulling discussions [1][2].
